subject: GenAPI latency surge: orchestration exceptions & customer note
messages:
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2028-09-14T08:13:00-07:00
Subject: [🔥] GenAPI p95 jump — immediate triage

Team —

We saw a sudden p95 latency increase (~3.2x baseline) on the Gen API starting 07:58 PDT across the us-west region. Impact window is ongoing but appears correlated with a higher-than-usual burst of short-sequence chat requests from a small customer cohort (FastCart). Initial signs point to routing congestion where some requests are being pinned to a suboptimal pooling group (fractional capacity nodes with older kernels).

What I have so far:
- Observed: p50 ~ stable, p95 jumped from 220ms -> ~720ms for token generation path. Throughput (rps) steady; CPU/GPU utilization uneven across pods.
- Suspected cause: router affinity rules + recent autoscaling tweak (last deploy 2028-09-13) causing uneven assignment to legacy node pool.
- Short-term mitigation attempted: manual reweighting of routing table pushed at 08:05 fixed a subset but the spike returned when traffic shifted.

Immediate asks:
1) Product: can we pause the recent routing affinity tweak while SRE gets a full dump? Need sign-off to roll back to pre-09-13 policy.
2) Sales/CS: hold a one-line ops note ready for FastCart (just a short acknowledgement).
3) Eng/SRE: I will collect KV cache stats and kernel selection traces; will share logs (query-sample-logs.txt) in a minute.

Attaching incident-timeline-20280914.pdf. Marking this P1 for customer-impacting workload.

Karthik
SRE Lead

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2028-09-14T08:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [🔥] GenAPI p95 jump — immediate triage

Thanks Karthik — good triage.

Marissa / Ben: we need two tracks in parallel:
- Tactical: approve rollback of the 09-13 routing affinity tweak for us-west to restore even distribution. SRE will need a 15-minute window to roll back and monitor.
- Customer comms: short transparent note to FastCart acknowledging we see increased latency, we are investigating with prioritized mitigation, and we'll follow up with a root-cause summary within 24 hours. No promises beyond transparency.

Product question for engineering (Karthik): if we roll back, what are the known trade-offs? Any risk to stability or throughput that we should call out to customer? Also: given this touches routing policy, is a longer-term exception (temporary dedicated routing for FastCart) feasible while we do a proper fix? If so, estimated ops delta and duration.

Ben, can you draft a one-paragraph acknowledgement to send to Marta (FastCart) — I'll review before you hit send. If Marissa approves the rollback, mark the customer comms as "pending mitigation" and include timing.

- Jonas
Product Manager

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2028-09-14T08:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [🔥] GenAPI p95 jump — immediate triage

Jonas — answers below.

Rollback trade-offs:
- Rolling back the 09-13 affinity tweak will restore round-robin distribution to all eligible pools. Expected p95 should trend back toward baseline within 5-12 minutes, based on previous rollout rollbacks.
- Risk: small chance of transient token-thrashing during rebalancing (~1-2 minutes) which could cause momentary p50 wobble; downstream queues may see ephemeral backpressure. We'll coordinate throttle windows.

Temporary dedicated routing for FastCart:
- Feasible as an exception. We can put a routing policy that pins FastCart's API key to the stable pool for up to 72 hours while we implement a proper fix. Ops cost: marginally higher (expected +6% unit GPU time) and requires a config-change with an emergency tag.
- Need product sign-off + legal OK if we prospectively apply credits (if SLA hit).

Plan of action (SRE):
1) Seek rollback approval from Product (Jonas) and Marissa for 08:55 PDT window.
2) If approved, roll back affinity tweak -> monitor; capture traces and KV cache dump.
3) If p95 normalizes, open a postmortem and propose the dedicated routing exception for 72h while eng implements kernel-selection guardrails.

I also attached query-sample-logs.txt (samples of requests hitting legacy nodes) to help narrow repro.

Karthik

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: marta.ortiz@fastcart.com
Cc: ops@fastcart.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-09-14T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Incident: increased latency impacting FastCart (acknowledgement)

Marta —

Thanks for flagging the latency you saw this morning. We’re investigating and have a priority ops action in flight to reduce latency; we’ll provide a short update once we’ve validated the mitigation.

Quick note for context: we’ve identified a routing policy change we rolled out yesterday that is likely contributing to uneven request assignment. We are pausing that change for us-west and expect to have an initial mitigation validated within ~20 minutes.

We’ll follow up within one hour with either confirmation that the issue is resolved or a brief note describing next steps. Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts your experience and are treating it as a priority.

— Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(bcc: internal ops thread)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2028-09-14T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: GenAPI latency surge: orchestration exceptions & customer note

Approved: rollback the 09-13 affinity tweak in the 08:55 slot (understood we missed the ideal window; proceed now). Also approve a 72-hour dedicated routing exception for FastCart while Eng implements a fix, provided we:
- Log the exception with tag EXC-2028-09-fastcart and auto-expire after 72 hours.
- Offer a one-time credit up to $2,000 if the SLA threshold was breached (Finance to finalize).

Ben: send the acknowledgement now and then follow with the mitigation confirmation once Karthik updates. Jonas: please own the postmortem and the product ask for kernel-selection guardrails; schedule a cross-team follow-up for tomorrow.

Marissa
VP, Platform Ops
